intro: Conflict arises when needs clash; handled early and calmly you can reduce tension, keep everyone safe, and protect the person's dignity.
points: Your safety comes first; if a situation feels unsafe, withdraw to a safe distance and call for help.
Never use physical restraint unless you are trained and it is a genuine last resort to prevent harm.
Treat challenging behaviour as communication of an unmet need, not a personal attack, and stay curious about the cause.
Keep calm: a low, warm voice, open body language and space often calm a person more than words.
Be assertive, not aggressive — state your needs clearly and respectfully while still valuing the other person.
Always record and report incidents and near misses, even when no one was physically injured.
